contract.description: The undo door of the memory system: bring back a memory whose earlier correction turned out wrong. Use it when you tombstoned a fact that is true again, or a newer memory superseded an older one that was right all along and the old truth must return. A restore is total: the record goes back to active with its tombstone lifted, and the superseding memory is tombstoned with reason "restored <id>" so exactly one active truth per fact remains. Repeating a restore is a safe no-op. An id that does not exist or lives in another tome comes back restored=false - an honest answer, not an error; writes never cross tomes. The response echoes the resolved tome and, when the record had a successor, where that superseder stands now. Every restore is recorded on the memory's correction trail with your reason, for the human to audit. upstream_unavailable means the store is unreachable and the reversal was not applied - the earlier correction stands. A crash between the two writes can leave the reversal half-applied; repeating the restore converges both sides.
contract.name: memory_restore
contract.title: Restore a memory
